findings.detail: Multiple rank/value mismatches: r15 GA=5.1% < r16 OR=5.6%; r20 NC=3.9% < r21 DE=4.9%; r24 KS=3.7% < r25 RI=3.8%; r27 OH=2.9% < r28 FL=3.2%; r33 IA=2.8% < r34 WI=3.2%; r39 AL=1.7% < r40 AR=1.9% < r41 NM=2.1%; r46 ME=1.7% < r47 VT=2.2%. Tail ordering is largely broken.
Tie at rank 8 uses '8.1% (tied)' for VA but plain '8.1%' for MA. Inconsistent tie-suffix formatting within the same question.
Covers all 50 states + DC; a 'smallest Asian population share' inverse (WV, MT, WY at bottom) would be a natural companion.

Multiple inversions: r17 OH=12.1% < r18 MI=13.6%; r25 OK=7.3% < r26 MA=7.5% < r27 NV=9.9% (NV should sit near r22); r32 NE=4.8% < r33 CA=5.6%; r34 CO=4.2% < r35 AZ=4.9%; r37 WA=4.0% < r38 IA=4.1%; r44 UT=1.5% < r45 ND=3.4%; r41 NM=2.6% > r42 OR=2.2% OK, but r40 HI=1.8% then NM=2.6% — inversion. Tail broken.
Covers 50+DC; inverse (lowest Black share — MT, ID, VT) is a natural companion.
Covers 50+DC monotonically; inverse (lowest veteran share — NY, NJ, DC at bottom) would be interesting.
r47 FL=7.4% < r48 WY=7.5%. WY should rank ahead of FL under descending sort.

Ranks 25, 25, 27 all show value '4' (NV, KY, NE). If three entries share the same value they should all be rank 25 (tied); assigning NE to rank 27 is inconsistent with the tie logic used elsewhere in the same question.

r18 OK=68,595 < r19 MO=68,742 (MO should outrank OK). Bottom of list has severe disorder: r43 HI=6,423 < r44 MA=7,800 < r45 VT=9,217 > r46 NH=8,953; correct descending order is MA (7,800)? actually MA<VT<NH — the true land-area ordering NH>VT>MA>HI is inverted here. Ranks 43-46 all mis-sorted.

Disclaimer explicitly discusses Michigan's Great Lakes waters. Michigan is rank 11 in Q15 (not top-5), so this is not a hard leak; but pairing this question with Q16 ('Land Area'), where the disclaimer again spotlights Michigan, telegraphs MI's presence/absence to players who see both questions. Minor.
